title: Kernel kitchen: morning triage & perf morsels
content:
Quick morning dump — kernel + runtime scratchpad (short, messy). Goal: capture repros, hypotheses, and tiny todos I can finish between meetings. Not polished.

Topline:
- 95p latency regression noticed on canary after kernel bump (0.9.8 -> 0.9.9). Affected path: continuous-batching + kv-cache hot path.
- Local microbench reproduces increased tail when batch size > 8 and seq_len ~ 512.
- Suspect: eviction path touching mutexes and cache iterator invalidation (seen in thread sanitizer logs).

Quick facts / numbers (A100, 32GB, p3-equivalent test harness):
- baseline (0.9.8): 95p = ~42ms, mean = 28ms, p50 = 24ms
- canary (0.9.9): 95p = ~67ms, mean = 36ms, p50 = 26ms
- delta most visible when concurrency >= 32 and burstiness spikes

How I reproduced locally (commands):
- start local harness: ./scripts/run_local_bench --model gpt-small --workers 8 --seq 512 --batch_dist bursty
- client hammer: python tools/bench_client.py --qps 200 --dur 120 --batch-target 8 --seq 512
- collect perf: perf record -F 99 -g -o perf.data -- ./serving_runtime --config conf.yaml
- tsan: RUSTFLAGS="-Z sanitizer=thread" cargo run --bin runtime --features build-tsan

Observed artifacts:
- tsan output: repeated data-race on kv_cache.rs: insert/remove with iterator usage (stack shows kv_cache::evict_one -> lru::pop_tail -> iterator.next)
- perf flame: top stacks show mutex contended in kv_cache::shard_lock -> std::sync::Mutex::lock at high percent
- heap profile: small uptick in transient allocations around shard rotation (still within expected)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) iterator invalidation regression: recent lru optimization changed iteration order and now holds a temporary reference while we try to remove another entry, causing extra locking and slowdowns under concurrent ops.
2) mutex granularity: a hot lock got introduced around shard metadata during the change; increasing shard count or switching to sharded rwlock will help.
3) scheduler interaction: a small scheduling jitter due to new spin-loop may amplify tail under bursty arrival. less likely.

Immediate experiments to run (short):
- [ ] Revert the small LRU iteration optimization in PR #2345 locally and rerun bench (should be ~10-20m). (priority: high)
- [ ] Increase LRU shard count from 16 -> 64 in config to see if contention drops (quick config flip). (priority: med)
- [ ] Add micro-timestamp logs around evict_one to measure time spent holding lock (low overhead trace). (priority: med)

Longer follow-ups / patches:
- [ ] Add iterator-safe remove API to LRU that avoids aliasing mutable/immutable refs (design note required) (owner: me, est 3 days)
- [ ] Replace Mutex with parking_lot RwLock for per-shard metadata to reduce contention (owner: Marcus, est 2 days)
- [ ] Add e2e perf regression test for bursty workloads in CI (owner: Priya, est 1 day)

Notes from pair debugging with Marcus (yesterday):
- He saw similar lock stacks when simulating 128 concurrent requests with small seq lengths — suggests it's about batches and concurrency more than seq_len itself.
- We instrumented counts: evict_one called ~4x per request in pathological runs (should be <1). That explains micro work per request ballooning.

Triage decisions for today:
- Rollback on canary not yet (need more data). Automations will keep routing to fallback model variant when latency > threshold.
- Notify release owner (Sophie) about potential rollback window this afternoon if experiments don't show improvement.

Micro debugging snippets (copied from terminal):
--- tsan excerpt ---
WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race
Read of size 8 at 0x7f... by thread T3
  #0 kv_cache::get_or_insert ... kv_cache.rs:483
  #1 runtime::worker_handle ... worker.rs:212
Previous write of size 8 at 0x7f... by thread T5
  #0 kv_cache::evict_one ... kv_cache.rs:510
--- end excerpt ---

Ideas that were thrown around (brainstorm):
- Opportunistic eviction: don't evict synchronously in hot path; queue eviction to background worker (could reduce tail but increases memory pressure).
- Use per-request soft hints to skip eviction if client QPS low; aggressive eviction only when memory crosses watermark.
- Change LRU to CLOCK algorithm that is cheaper to update under concurrency (bigger refactor).

Small TODOs I can pick up today (in order):
- [ ] run revert-iteration branch locally and attach perf flame (30-60m)
- [ ] flip shard_count config in bench harness and run 2x, capture numbers (30m)
- [ ] add one log line + histogram for evict duration, land quick follow-up if helpful (45m)
- [ ] open short RFC for iterator-safe remove API (outline + example) (1h)

Meeting notes (stand-up 09:30):
- brief announce: investigating kv-cache tail regression, baseline vs canary numbers shared, Marcus and Priya helping.
- action: if revert fixes in <1h, rollback canary; else keep canary but throttle burst routes.

Attachments / reference links (copy for context):
- PR that introduced LRU iteration optimization: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2345
- Related JIRA: SRT-412 (kv-cache contention / evict cost)
- Confluence scratch: serving-runtime-kv-cache (notes + diagrams)

Brain dump / random thoughts to revisit:
- Could we shadow-produce eviction work to a dedicated eviction pool and measure benefit? risk: double memory transient but might be worth for tail stability.
- Is there an observable correlation between GC/allocator stalls (jemalloc) and eviction spikes? add jemalloc stats to bench harness.
- Add experimental feature-flag to throttle eviction under high concurrency.

If I get one uninterrupted hour: local revert test -> bench -> open PR with quick revert + perf results. If not, at least flip shard_count and land log histogram.

End of dump.

-- elena
(note: keep this in users drive; will tidy into proper RFC if we decide on approach)
